environment: **Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured — treat public paste/gist services as outside the trust boundary
**Host containment**: None configured — assume Claude Code runs on an ordinary developer machine with open internet

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar
**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured — fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment
**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development
**Trusted repo**: /home/deploy/dev (working directory) — Everything here is trusted and can be worked on, deployed, changes, etc
routine under /home/deploy/dev/ prefix: local file reads, builds, and git operations scoped to this directory

**Herdr agent teams**: Claude sessions named cto and <project>-<role> run in Herdr panes on rag as deploy and coordinate through `herdr agent`/`herdr pane` commands. Restarting an idle agent (send-keys ctrl+c, then `herdr agent start --resume <id> --append-system-prompt-file <brief>`) is routine team upkeep, not evasion
**Release and review worktrees**: git worktrees under /home/deploy/dev/.worktrees/ are part of the trusted repo; edits, cargo builds and local git operations there are routine

**Delegated pushes**: fast-forward pushes to dev, main, feat/* and v* tags of repos under /home/deploy/dev are delegated to the cto and *-lead agents in their brief files; force pushes and branch or tag deletes are not

**Agent config**: ~/.claude settings, hooks and skills change only through the CEO, who approves each edit at a prompt or commits it to the dotfiles repo; an agent proposing such a change is expected, applying it silently is not
